source_documents.title: Quantitative Design of Bright Fluorophores and AIEgens via the Accurate Prediction of Twisted Intramolecular Charge Transfer (TICT)

reference_evidence_units.quote: the quantum yields of P4 (Φ = 0.38) and P5 (Φ = 0.33) are about twice than that of P2 (Φ = 0.17)
reference_evidence_units.subject: P2, P4
reference_evidence_units.statement: Azetidine P4 doubles the yield of dimethylamino P2.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the enhancement of fluorescence intensities of P2 and P4 can be attributed to TICT inhibition as glycerol is significantly more viscous and less polar than water
reference_evidence_units.subject: P2, P4
reference_evidence_units.statement: Glycerol inhibits TICT (viscosity and polarity covary).

reference_evidence_units.quote: While P4 is also prone to the TICT formation, it exhibited much stronger “TICT resistance”.
reference_evidence_units.subject: P2 vs P4
reference_evidence_units.statement: Higher rotation barrier in P4 (0.38 vs 0.23 eV).

reference_evidence_units.quote: suggesting the co-existence of the non-emissive TICT (τ1 = 79 ps) and emissive ICT (τ2 = 1.37 ns) states.
reference_evidence_units.subject: P4 (P2 similar)
reference_evidence_units.statement: Non-emissive TICT (79 ps) coexists with emissive ICT.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Viscous glycerol inhibits the TICT rotation (polarity covaries).

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: P2: non-emissive N-TICT formation competes with emissive ICT in water; P4's azetidine raises the barrier.
